The opening 20 minutes of the match were already full of sparks, with neither side giving an inch. After the hydration break, each team had a player shown a yellow card — England midfielder Elliot Anderson and Argentina centre-back Lisandro Martínez. Before the end of the first half, fans cheered for their own side whenever the referee blew the whistle and booed the opposition's fouls.

The first half ended level, and after the teams switched ends, England's Anthony Gordon received a pass in the 55th minute to break the deadlock and give England a 1-0 lead. England fans in the venue immediately erupted in celebration.

Trailing by a goal, Argentina launched an immediate counter-attack. Within 10 minutes they launched three attacks down the right with crosses, but the ball was cleared inside the penalty area each time, drawing sighs from Argentina supporters. It was not until the 85th minute that Enzo Fernández headed in a cross from Messi to level the scores at 1-1, sending Argentina fans into a frenzy as the sound of drums and horns filled the air.

In stoppage time, in the 92nd minute, Messi set up Lautaro Martínez to score the winning goal, helping Argentina knock out England and advance to the final, where they will face Spain for the World Cup title. Argentina fans in the venue once again erupted in jubilation. When the final whistle blew, fans continued to embrace in celebration, with some even holding up cardboard cutouts of Messi that they had picked up at the mall.

Argentina fan Aho said he had been supporting Messi since the latter made his name at Barcelona. Wearing an Argentina number 10 jersey printed with "two stars", he said this World Cup would be Messi's last and that the national team was also defending its title. Messi's and the team's path to the championship has generated considerable controversy during the tournament, but Aho believed that rather than getting bogged down in the standard of refereeing at every match, it was better to cherish the few remaining days of Messi playing for his country. He laughed and said that, while he was still young enough, he had chosen to stay up overnight at the mall to watch the match with other fans.

England fans have been singing "Football's coming home!" throughout the tournament, only to once again fail to bring football home. Deakin, who is studying in the United Kingdom, returned to Hong Kong during the summer break. Today, draped in an England flag, he cheered wholeheartedly for his beloved team alongside friends during the intense battle between the two sides. He said it was his first time watching a match at a mall and experiencing the atmosphere, adding that fans were very enthusiastic but also respectful of one another, with no overly heated clashes breaking out.

A defeat for their beloved team inevitably brought disappointment. Deakin, who shares a name with England midfielder Declan Rice, said England had performed well in this match. A fan of two World Cups, he said frankly: "We've waited 60 years; waiting another four years is no big deal!"

Argentina will face Spain on the 20th as they bid to defend their title. In the third-place playoff, England will take on France on the 19th.
